method: hand_calculation and interface reasoning; not an additional experiment

steps.topic: Why target CE cannot be an online signal
steps.details: For class probabilities p and actual class y, CE(p,y)=-log(p_y). The same p can occur with y=0 or y=1, so p alone does not determine actual-target CE. A pseudo-label CE is computable but is a different quantity and does not recover hidden y.

A fixed b(q)=k, a user choice b(q,u)=mapping(u), or an upfront b(q)=g(features(q)) can be evaluated without y, provided the features themselves are available at serving time. Select/freeze k, mapping, or g on validation; this says nothing about whether a chosen budget will be optimal for an unseen item. The lesson introduces these choices as baselines and the first Auto design; it reports no implementation or measured quality.

steps.topic: Artificial stable wrong result and arbitrary confidence threshold
steps.details: In the stated example, 0.95>0.05 and 0.97>0.03, so argmax is 0 both rounds; y=1 makes both wrong. At threshold 0.9, round 1 immediately stops wrong. More generally, for any strict confidence threshold t in [0,1), let p=((3+t)/4,(1-t)/4) and y=1. The entries are nonnegative and sum to 1; p0-t=3(1-t)/4>0 and p0-p1=(1+t)/2>0. Identical copies across rounds make the answer stable and confidently wrong. No higher usable threshold can guarantee correctness without distributional assumptions. A threshold exceeding or equal to 1 with strict > may simply never stop. Even ideal calibration concerns conditional frequencies, not correctness of each individual item.

If low is executed and high is then independently rerun, both executed jobs belong in the total work/time accounting (also any selector overhead). Peak memory is measured rather than summed. Reusing a previous latent state is a different interface: the state, phase/position and any cache must match the model recurrence; it is not implied by offering low/high settings. ACT eq. (3) explicitly makes subsequent recurrence depend on the preceding state; this supports the state prerequisite, not a universal cache API.

For a fixed saved evaluation run i=1..n, finite candidate rounds R, and the SAME score Q_i(r), define Q_i*=max_{r in R}Q_i(r). Every controller selecting g_i in R satisfies Q_i(g_i)<=Q_i* pointwise, hence mean_i Q_i(g_i)<=mean_i Q_i*. For loss, min_{r in R}L_i(r) is instead a lower bound on loss. For accuracy Q_i(r)=1[pred_i(r)=y_i], the retrospective per-item best is an accuracy upper bound only within these saved candidates. Minimum CE and maximum answer accuracy need not choose the same round. The bound ignores selection/rollout cost and does not show a realizable label-free controller, new random rollouts, or new data will attain it.

scope: Transparent derivations supporting only the lesson’s restrictions; no empirical effect or speed claim.
